elements.title: Active festival after-rating compatibility
elements.description: Reads only the current active festival
elements.overview: Read-only RealRatingRepository compatibility for existing detail and legacy export consumers. Resolves the active festival before querying its after-rating port; never selects the latest event or another festival. save deliberately refuses writes.

elements.title: Festival creation worker
elements.description: Runs creation away from the UI
elements.overview: Runs the creation Supplier supplied by ImportCsvActivity on its worker executor and delivers either AddFestivalResult or a failure message through the supplied UI executor. It does not decide identities or write data; the composed command invokes AddFestivalUseCase.

elements.title: Festival lifecycle use cases
elements.description: Add, rename, archive, and enter festivals
elements.overview: Orchestrates active-festival transitions, validates new festival input, and prepares the start state and results presented by Android screens.

elements.title: Android application
elements.overview: Installed Android process running Activities, application workflows, domain rules, repository, Room and TSV adapters. Reads owned on-device cache and synchronizes through the external Supabase platform. Gradle modules are packaged code, not separate runtimes.

elements.title: Android composition root
elements.overview: Constructs Room adapters and chooses Supabase or explicit TSV fallback sources; exposes repositories and pending-sync state to Android entry points.

elements.title: Archived festival screen
elements.overview: Displays an archived festival lineup and opens read-only band details.

elements.title: Reviewed archived correction dialog
elements.overview: ArchivedBandDetailActivity opens this dialog with a supplied correction use case. Loads member/festival/band/kind and revision; stages locally then explicitly confirms planning zero-to-five or after one-to-five. Stable payload-derived operation ID supports uncertain-result retry, stale review requires reload, and lifecycle generation guards ignore obsolete UI completions.

elements.title: Archived correction review contract
elements.overview: Port with ArchivedRatingKind and immutable ArchivedRatingReview values: these are one correction protocol, not separate runtime components. Review/correct/history preserve exact owner and target, expected revision and original recorded date. Adapter/server enforce atomic audit and current-source protection.

elements.title: Correct own archived rating
elements.overview: Validates signed-in owner, archived selected festival and lineup. Review response must match member/festival/band/kind; correction validates operation UUID and scale before invoking the gateway. Does not implement server revision/audit/provenance policy in the UI.

elements.title: Archive screen worker
elements.overview: MainActivity supplies AppRepositories.archiveFestivalUseCase through a Supplier. Executes it on the worker and returns success/failure on the UI executor; does not itself choose promotion or persistence rules.

elements.title: Local auth session
elements.description: Persist and expose the signed-in session
elements.overview: Stores the current Supabase user and group context on device so app workflows can address shared and personal records.

elements.title: Band catalog model
elements.overview: Models reusable bands and the rule that hides generic Metal Battle placeholders from rating views while preserving imported records.

elements.title: Band detail screens
elements.description: Present band information and personal ratings
elements.overview: Presents active and archived band information with the captured member/festival scope, established source/history context and read-only group planning summaries. Active editing puts planning first and keeps the independent post-show value behind a retained After the show disclosure. Owns the reusable native rating choices and shared meaning vocabulary used by detail and lineup: touch, keyboard and accessibility actions use the existing callbacks/use cases, while archived children remain disabled. Restyling and recreation retain views/state without replaying rating events; actual biography, images, performance context and stored music links are preserved. Canonical-band discovery retains its existing no-festival entry but is absent in captured archive context; archived corrections keep their explicit reviewed workflow.

elements.title: Band image request owner
elements.overview: Owns one background image request for a detail screen, including 5-second connect/inactive-read limits, stream closure and HTTP disconnect. Replacing a target or destroying its owner cancels the current request and invalidates queued callbacks. Bitmap decoding and view updates stay with the Android screen; failures and null decode use its missing-image fallback. Does not read or write ratings, metadata or festival lifecycle state.

elements.title: Band link review screen
elements.overview: Presents own-catalog matches for imported band names in full-width vertical rows. Labeled native search and match controls retain edited terms, explicit No match or chosen canonical name and viewport through recreation; search changes require a current match choice. Both palettes use the shared focused input/selector styling. Only the existing explicit link action invokes the application linker; searching, theme changes and restoration do not rename or merge bands or change ratings.

elements.title: Metadata review screen
elements.overview: Displays missing fields, provider status, candidate values, clickable source URLs and explicit accepted-metadata results in the paired native layout. A retained screen session owns its existing read-only search worker, result and checked proposals so recreation does not repeat in-flight lookup or discard review. Cancel interrupts unfinished search and preserves saved data; results after cancellation are discarded and retry is explicit. Shared48dp choices, live status and wrapping evidence preserve large-text reachability. Existing search/apply use cases retain missing-field and no-overwrite authority; only Save accepted metadata applies checked proposals.

elements.title: Domain repository ports
elements.description: Storage contracts for festival planning data
elements.overview: Defines the domain-facing access contracts for bands, festivals, lineups, ratings, performances, stages, distances, food, and personal history. Implementations are supplied by Room, Supabase, or file adapters.

elements.title: Reviewed canonical band identity
elements.overview: Defines the stable catalog ID/metadata value, confirmed alias provenance and reviewed uploaded-name selection. Alias keys fold ASCII case and spacing only, retaining punctuation and non-ASCII spelling. A new-band choice has no selected canonical value; remembering an alias requires an explicit selection. These values support identity review, not automatic fuzzy merging.

elements.title: Festival deletion confirmation
elements.overview: Shown from active home or archived festival views. Requires explicit deletion confirmation, then invokes AppRepositories.deleteFestival on a worker and returns success/error on the UI thread. Explains removal of festival-scoped data and retention of canonical bands/personal history. The backend owns authorization and atomic deletion; local cleanup follows acknowledged remote success.

elements.title: Festival deletion use case
elements.overview: Resolves the requested festival from the repository and invokes its configured Gateway; missing festivals require refresh. AppRepositories binds SupabaseFestivalDeletionGateway, separating application selection from remote deletion and local cache cleanup.

elements.title: Own correction audit CSV export
elements.overview: Separate audit-only contract reads the signed-in member corrections and emits stable operation/target/kind/old/new and original/correction timestamps. Retains festival-name snapshots after deletion; does not replace either legacy ratings CSV or lifecycle version2 export.

elements.title: Own rating lifecycle CSV export
elements.overview: Version2 own cached contract includes established provenance, exact festival planning/after-state, dated history and immutable corrections as distinct record types. Unknown dates remain blank, missing differs from zero and deleted festival provenance survives. Sorted/escaped rows do not promote latest events; legacy CSV remains a separate Settings action.

elements.title: Rating CSV export
elements.overview: Collects local planning ratings, post-show ratings, group rating details, and available schedule metadata into a CSV payload for Android sharing.

elements.title: Festival attendee
elements.overview: Rates bands, reviews a shared conflict-aware schedule, records personal post-show ratings, and browses archived festivals.

elements.title: Festival data admin
elements.overview: Imports validated festival CSVs and reviews possible band links and metadata before saving them.

elements.title: Festival lifecycle model
elements.overview: Models an active or archived festival and its lineup entries, including lifecycle constraints used when a festival is archived or added.

elements.title: Festival after-rating contract
elements.overview: Domain port and immutable FestivalAfterRating values keyed by member, festival and canonical band. Operation identity supports replay; zero is a durable reset, and requiresReview marks uncertain migrated facts. Recording never establishes the reusable personal band opinion.

elements.title: Selected festival after-rating view
elements.overview: Read-only compatibility adapter to the festival after-rating port. Both active and archive screens can pin their selected festival. Does not write or fall back to the currently active festival.

elements.title: Atomic festival archive port
elements.overview: Application output contract invoked by ArchiveActiveFestivalUseCase. AppRepositories supplies a pre-syncing callback which verifies no pending work before delegating to the remote archive adapter. Missing/reset after-ratings retain established values; actual atomic promotion is implemented by SQL V016.

elements.title: Festival identity review port
elements.overview: Application read port returning immutable canonical band and confirmed-alias snapshots. ReviewFestivalBandsUseCase consumes fresh catalog data; Android composition supplies SupabaseFestivalBandCatalog. A failed read must prevent presenting incomplete choices as authoritative.

elements.title: Festival identity confirmation
elements.overview: Presents proposals from ReviewFestivalBandsUseCase. Exact canonical names retain exact reuse; suggestions and aliases require an explicit choice to reuse a band or create a separate band. Alias remembrance is opt-in. Only the final summary confirmation invokes the callback supplied by ImportCsvActivity; cancellation creates no festival or alias.

elements.title: Atomic festival creation port
elements.overview: Application write port for atomic group-wide creation. The transaction checks authoritative active-festival state, reuses reviewed canonical identities and copies each existing member's established band rating once into a new planning snapshot. Missing opinions stay unrated and after-ratings start empty. Only the creator's planning snapshot is returned. Retry confirms the same creation without resetting edits. SupabaseFestivalCreationGateway is supplied by Android composition.

elements.title: Festival CSV parsing
elements.overview: Shared application CSV reader for lineup names and local master-data review. Supplies parsed rows/headers and format errors before writes; callers own group-wide creation versus local five-file acceptance. Parsing does not confirm canonical identity or mutate ratings.

elements.title: Selected festival planning view
elements.overview: Implements the planning compatibility port for a fixed selected festival. Reads only that festival and validates it remains active and the band remains in its lineup before saving. Uses the composed planning repository, retaining pending offline edits.

elements.title: Festival-scoped performance view
elements.overview: Wraps a caller-selected PerformanceRepository with a festival ID supplied by AppRepositories. Reads only that festival, rejects writes for another festival and refuses global replaceAll. Explicit master-data import uses the unscoped target. This adapter preserves active/archive scope without copying or deleting another festival's performances.

elements.title: TSV fallback adapters
elements.overview: Reads and writes app-private TSV data for the explicit fallback import/source mode; this path is separate from the default Supabase source.

elements.title: Verify and approve missing music links
elements.overview: Application workflow selects missing fields within one band or festival lineup, retains completed searches and retries unfinished work. Verifies matching MusicBrainz/Wikidata artist identifiers, Group identity/name or aliases, jointly declared official site and unique linked platform profile. Ranking or caller-supplied checkbox alone is insufficient. Approval rechecks raw evidence/current band, refuses ambiguous/conflicting identities and delegates only missing YouTube/Spotify fields to existing metadata proposal application; no rating or lineup write port is supplied.

elements.title: Shared schedule generation
elements.overview: Reads performances, group ratings, and stage distances, applies domain conflict decisions, and returns day and slot projections for the calendar.

elements.title: CSV import screen
elements.overview: Receives Android document selections and invokes the CSV import workflow for lineup and related festival data.

elements.title: CSV import values and initial band import
elements.description: Shares reviewed CSV input/result values and retains the initial band-list API
elements.overview: Owns FestivalCsvFiles and ImportFestivalCsvResult, which the active ReviewFestivalCsvUseCase uses, alongside the separate ImportInitialBandListUseCase and its result. The unused full ImportFestivalCsvUseCase was removed in TASK-228. Its deleted source reference was detached through the CLI after scanning retained it. Groma still stores authored relationships to that deleted file; these are known stale claims, pending safe relationship-removal tooling support. Current Android five-file imports use explicit row review and the TSV/Room transaction.

elements.title: Band and history queries
elements.description: Read active and archived festival views
elements.overview: Builds band list and detail projections, including archived festival history and per-person rating details, from repository data.

elements.title: Local CSV acceptance review
elements.overview: Displays ReviewFestivalCsvUseCase before/after/error rows with unchecked defaults and explicit valid-row acceptance. Retained state stores data/work without an Activity; fresh lifecycle callbacks render status and detach safely. Apply invokes the application use case once with selected keys, protects in-flight work and reports local success or retained-data errors. Cancel does not save. Shared sync may later refresh this local cache.

elements.title: Login screen
elements.overview: Collects credentials and starts a Supabase Auth session before the planning screens are entered.

elements.title: Festival home screen
elements.description: Show active lineup and archived start state
elements.overview: Presents the actual alphabetically scoped active lineup with wrapping band, planning-rating meaning and performance context, local name search and an Unrated filter. Its presentation helper filters existing display items without owning rating or festival policy. Keeps query, filter and selected-row context through detail return and recreation, opens only stored music links, and exposes cached/offline retry and archive/add-next entry states. Planning saves and festival lifecycle actions use the existing application use cases; primary destinations use shared stateless navigation.

elements.title: Primary destination navigation
elements.overview: Builds the same labeled Bands, Schedule and Settings destination bar around each primary screen, exposing the current destination visually and to accessibility services. Selecting the current Activity is a no-op; another destination is opened with Android Intent REORDER_TO_FRONT so an existing Activity retains its screen context rather than creating duplicate navigation instances. Detail and review subflows keep their initiating Activity and normal Back behavior. Shared appearance helpers style the controls; this component owns no rating, schedule, session or persistence policy.

elements.title: Member planning-rating projection
elements.overview: Projects an already festival-scoped planning snapshot by exact canonical band name, retains positive values including veto stars and preserves stable case-insensitive member ordering. List, detail, schedule and CSV workflows reuse this read-only transformation. Repository selection, archive scope, decision rules and CSV formatting remain in their existing owners; after-ratings and established ratings are not substituted.

elements.title: Missing festival pending context
elements.overview: Typed adapter exception identifies the exact SavedFestivalPlanningRating blocked by an unavailable festival. The recovery dialog discovers it through the exception chain; ordinary sync failure does not silently discard or reassign the fact.

elements.title: Review orphaned pending rating
elements.overview: Home/Settings sync failure opens this dialog only for the typed missing-festival error. Keep is default; move and separately confirmed discard call AppRepositories recovery commands on a worker. Successful recovery retries sync; failures report that pending work remains.

elements.title: MusicBrainz
elements.overview: Provides artist candidates and official URL relationships for reviewed metadata proposals.

elements.title: MusicBrainz provider
elements.description: Propose artist identity and music links
elements.overview: Searches artist candidates and URL relationships to propose canonical identity, Spotify, or YouTube links for review.

elements.title: Music identity evidence contract
elements.overview: Lookup port and immutable MusicLinkEvidence/Page values form one protocol. Candidates contain artist identifiers, corroborating source facts, declared websites and extracted platform links with retry/messages; these facts are not a verification decision. The application verifies them, distinct from general ranked BandMetadataProviderCandidate proposals.

elements.title: Verified music link review screen
elements.description: Reviews missing links before explicit save
elements.overview: Settings supplies active festival ID or BandDetailActivity supplies one canonical band name. Retained worker/session preserves completed reviews, terms and approval choices across rotation; cancellation interrupts unfinished lookup. Paired48dp inputs/choices and wrapping source buttons expose canonical URLs and identity rationale. Editing terms immediately removes stale evidence/approval controls without rebuilding the input, never renames bands and requires a fresh search. Only verified selected identity plus explicit acknowledgement enables save. Search may be public, while save uses the captured account-bound shared repository; no claim is made that an account switch automatically cancels public lookup.

elements.title: Official artist websites
elements.overview: Public artist homepages declared by both MusicBrainz and Wikidata supply outgoing platform profile links as corroborating evidence. Bounded public HTTPS retrieval does not execute scripts or send credentials. Application identity and unique-profile checks plus explicit user approval remain required before canonical missing links are saved.

elements.title: Bounded official artist page reader
elements.overview: PageLoader used by the evidence collector retrieves public HTTPS HTML with five-second connect/read timeouts,512KiB limit and at most three redirects. Each destination is revalidated; private/local addresses, credentials, nonstandard ports and non-HTML responses fail. Uses no cookies, proxy, scripts or automatic redirects and checks interruption. Parsed anchors are evidence only; the application still verifies declared site and unique profile links.

elements.title: On-device cache
elements.overview: Owned on-device wacken-cache.db storage. Room entities, DAOs, migrations and repositories execute inside the Android application; this storage boundary does not own their Java source. WackenDatabase.get opens the cache through Room.databaseBuilder. The Java scanner does not model storage execution.

elements.title: Festival schedule model
elements.overview: Represents scheduled band appearances and stage context used by lineup and schedule workflows.

elements.title: Schedule decision rules
elements.description: Conflict detection and group choice policy
elements.overview: Detects overlapping performances and applies group preferences, vetoes, optional choices, and walking-time context to decide schedule candidates.

elements.title: Established personal band opinion contract
elements.overview: Read-only domain access and provenance-bearing PersonalBandRating values. Each member has their own opinion; source festival/name/event survive deletion. Nonempty archive promotion and eligible current-source correction are the write mechanisms, rather than latest-event fallback or normal detail edits.

elements.title: Rating use cases
elements.overview: Orchestrates planning rating changes, effective group rating lookup, and separate real post-show personal rating history.

elements.title: Rating model
elements.overview: Represents the one-to-five rating scale, saved planning ratings, and personal rating events retained with festival and creation context.

elements.title: Correction audit contract
elements.overview: Repository port and RatingCorrection value expose own audit by user or exact festival/band. Stable operation, old/new values, reviewed revision, original recorded time and correction time are distinct. History survives festival deletion; it is not a source for latest-event band opinion promotion.

elements.title: After-rating state synchronization
elements.description: Pushes pending and pulls own snapshots
elements.overview: AppRepositories invokes this coordinator. Pushes explicit pending facts before acknowledging the exact operation, skips migrated facts needing review, then fetches both complete own after-rating and established-opinion snapshots before cache merge. Exceptions preserve pending work; established state is read from the server.

elements.title: Rating sync cache port
elements.overview: Extends the after-rating domain port with pending enumeration, exact operation acknowledgement, own after-state merge and established-opinion replacement. RoomFestivalAfterRatingRepository implements this adapter-facing protocol.

elements.title: Record festival after-rating
elements.overview: Checks active festival and lineup membership, validates zero-to-five, then saves an operation-identified assessment with original clock time. Zero persists a reset. No planning or established-opinion write port is supplied.

elements.title: Recover orphaned pending planning rating
elements.overview: Moves only a reviewed own pending fact whose original festival is missing to active Wacken2026, with local and remote no-overwrite checks and exact stale-state protection. Explicit discard similarly validates owner and unchanged pending fact. Otherwise retains work; does not automatically reassign festivals or change lifecycle rules.

elements.title: Festival identity proposals
elements.overview: Loads the FestivalBandCatalog snapshot, rejects duplicate exact canonical names, and proposes exact matches plus alias/name-similarity suggestions for uploaded names. It never silently chooses a fuzzy/alias match, creates a band or merges ratings. FestivalBandReviewDialog owns human confirmation; domain identity values retain the selected canonical ID and alias choice.

elements.title: Local five-file import review
elements.overview: Builds before/after/error rows for five optional CSV inputs against an active-festival snapshot. Accepted keys are explicit and initially unchecked; missing companion files retain their baseline. Before publish it validates combined references/overlaps and rechecks stale data inside the supplied transaction. It retains canonical catalog metadata, other festivals, ratings/history and pending work; removing a lineup entry does not delete a canonical band. AppRepositories supplies TSV fallback decorators and TsvImportTransaction with Room callback. This is local master-data review, not a shared-source import API.

elements.title: Imported band linking
elements.overview: Identifies likely catalog matches for imported names and applies an explicit user-reviewed band link.

elements.title: Room correction publication
elements.overview: Captures exact pending operation/value and validates acknowledged member/festival/band/kind before transactional publication. Refuses newer pending edits; resolves only the reviewed pending fact, merges snapshots and appends immutable audit together. Original offline history date remains separate from correction time.

elements.title: Confirmed alias cache
elements.overview: Owns Room alias row, DAO and mapping behind one local persistence responsibility. Reads aliases with canonical identity and member/time provenance; replaceAll clears and saves the complete acknowledged snapshot in one Room transaction. SupabaseFestivalBandCatalog publishes fresh authenticated aliases through the callback bound in AppRepositories. It does not confirm or invent an alias.

elements.title: Room festival after-rating cache
elements.description: Persists pending assessments and durable resets
elements.overview: Adapter and RoomFestivalAfterRating row form one cache responsibility. save writes PENDING after-state and a dated history fact only for nonzero values in a Room transaction. Merge replaces own synced state while retaining newer pending rows; acknowledgement matches operation identity. Established snapshots are replaced only for the authenticated owner.

elements.title: Room archive publication
elements.overview: Consumer supplied by AppRepositories to the archive gateway. Rechecks pending work inside the Room transaction, merges own after-state and established snapshot, and saves the acknowledged archived festival together. Newly pending edits prevent local overwrite; remote success is retained as a recovery outcome.

elements.title: Festival cache initialization marker
elements.overview: Owns the initialization-marker Room entity and DAO. RoomFestivalRepository and acknowledged deletion mark initialization so an intentionally empty/deleted festival cache is not mistaken for first launch and reseeded. Count/insert-ignore are storage mechanics, not a second festival or runtime.

elements.title: Acknowledged creation cache
elements.overview: Consumes the validated creation snapshot supplied by SupabaseFestivalCreationGateway through AppRepositories. Within one WackenDatabase Room transaction it publishes festivals, canonical metadata, lineup, creator-only planning values and acknowledged aliases. Existing pending planning edits for that festival/member are retained. Other members' private history or planning snapshots are not returned or fabricated.

elements.title: Festival cache deletion
elements.overview: Runs after remote deletion acknowledgement. One Room transaction detaches retained personal history with festival name, removes selected festival planning/after state, lineup, performances, locks and festival record, and marks the cache initialized. Canonical bands and established personal band ratings are retained. It does not independently authorize group-wide deletion.

elements.title: Room established opinion reader
elements.overview: Read-only adapter and RoomPersonalBandRating row expose current own opinion and its source festival/name/event/date. Uses shared RoomRatingStateDao; normal application rating edits do not write established opinions.

elements.title: Room correction audit cache
elements.overview: Repository adapter, RoomRatingCorrection row and DAO form one audit cache responsibility. Maps full provenance and original/correction timestamps; appends by operation identity and reads owner/target histories. Separate from mutable after-state and current established snapshot tables.

elements.title: Room rating state queries
elements.description: Separates pending after-state and established snapshots
elements.overview: Shared Room query interface for after-ratings and established band opinions. Exact member/festival/band predicates and operation-matched acknowledgement preserve scopes. Keeping this shared query responsibility separate avoids assigning it exclusively to either reader or writer.

elements.title: Schedule calendar screen
elements.description: Present and adjust the group timeline
elements.overview: Renders the day-filtered stage/time calendar and its existing generated decisions. Labeled native day and threshold selectors, a wrapping barred-overlap control and a readable key retain local filters, focus and calendar position across rerenders, appearance changes and recreation, including empty results. Calendar geometry scales with text while essential horizontal scrolling stays inside the timeline; full date, stage, time, rank, scratch and lock meanings remain available through native accessibility and the wrapping decision dialog. Both palettes restyle the existing grid, rank outlines, scratch marks and walking context. Restored dialogs wait for cached group locks and retain the actual chosen act. Alternative selection still uses the existing local manual-selection and pending group-lock paths without changing personal ratings, generated evidence, ties, day cutoff or walking rules.

elements.title: Metadata proposal workflow
elements.overview: Finds missing band fields, proposes own-catalog and provider values, and applies only accepted values without overwriting populated metadata.

elements.title: Settings screen
elements.description: Launch import, review, export, and sync actions
elements.overview: Provides grouped appearance, account/group, festival administration, rating export/allocation and manual sync actions. Link imported bands and active-festival music discovery are adjacent in festival administration; canonical-band discovery stays on detail. Shared headings, readable wrapping body text and live status use the selected palette, and the Settings scroll position survives recreation. Import, rename, export, invite and pending-sync behavior still delegate to the existing workflows.

elements.title: Shared planner database
elements.overview: Owned planner schema, canonical catalog, member-scoped ratings, archive/correction RPCs and RLS, hosted by Supabase. SQL evidence is in backend/flyway/sql and ADR0016. Supabase Auth and hosted PostgREST belong to the external platform. Java-only analysis does not inspect the SQL.

elements.title: Spotify
elements.overview: Provides optional artist profile and image candidates when credentials are configured.

elements.title: Spotify provider
elements.overview: When credentials are configured, searches the Spotify catalog for artist profile and image candidates for review.

elements.title: Supabase
elements.overview: Provides Auth and PostgREST access to shared festival master data, planning ratings, personal rating history, and group schedule locks.

elements.title: Authenticated correction gateway
elements.overview: Uniquely resolves canonical band, checks authenticated owner, captures pending state, submits reviewed revision and stable operation to correct_archived_rating, validates receipt, then reloads current target and private snapshots before cache publication. SQL V017 commits immutable audit with eligible established update only while this festival remains current source; planning and older-source corrections cannot promote. Paged audit refresh checks every owner.

elements.title: Supabase authentication adapter
elements.description: Sign in and refresh authenticated sessions
elements.overview: Calls Supabase Auth, manages session lifecycle, and reports invalid or missing authentication to app workflows.

elements.title: Authenticated HTTP transport
elements.overview: Adds configuration and session credentials to HTTP requests and reports backend failures used by remote repository adapters.

elements.title: Authenticated festival archive gateway
elements.overview: Invokes archive_festival via the composed authenticated request callback, validates selected festival and operation acknowledgement, then fetches complete own rating snapshots before invoking the Room cache callback. SQL V016 atomically archives and promotes each member nonempty after-state; missing/reset retains opinions and replay preserves later state. Remote commit followed by local failure is explicitly recoverable.

elements.title: Remote identity review catalog
elements.overview: Implements FestivalBandCatalog through authenticated paged bands/alias reads using SupabaseMasterDataClient. Builds canonical identity values and replaces the Room alias cache only after a complete successful alias fetch via the callback supplied by AppRepositories. Errors retain prior cached aliases and require retry; cached suggestions are not silent approval.

elements.title: Shared festival creation adapter
elements.overview: Implements FestivalCreationGateway. Sends a deterministic request identity and reviewed canonical/alias choices to create_festival_from_reviewed_bands through SupabaseMasterDataClient; exact legacy creation remains supported. Validates acknowledged member/group, festival, lineup and aliases before delivering the snapshot to the RoomFestivalCreationCache callback bound by AppRepositories. Server creation is atomic under SQL V018 and its existing V015 creation transaction; each member is seeded once and new after-ratings stay empty. A remote success followed by cache failure is reported as shared-saved/local-refresh-needed, never rolled back or falsely called wholly failed. Retry uses the same name, CSV and choices; stale identities require review. SQL/RLS semantics are authored evidence, not Java scanner inference.

elements.title: Shared festival deletion adapter
elements.overview: Implements the deletion use-case Gateway supplied by AppRepositories. Calls SupabaseMasterDataClient.deleteFestival first, then the supplied RoomFestivalDeletion callback. Remote errors leave local state intact; local cleanup failure after acknowledged remote deletion reports shared success with sync recovery needed. SQL V011 owns authorization, transactional scope and preservation of canonical bands/history.

elements.title: Supabase master data adapters
elements.description: Read and write shared festival records
elements.overview: Uses Supabase PostgREST for band, stage, performance, distance, food, festival, and lineup records.

elements.title: Supabase shared state adapters
elements.overview: Uses authenticated Supabase endpoints for group planning ratings, personal rating history, and locked schedule winners.

elements.title: Authenticated rating state client
elements.description: Saves operations and reads own state
elements.overview: Implements RatingStateSync.Remote through authenticated SupabaseMasterDataClient requests. Uniquely resolves canonical band ID, invokes save_festival_after_rating with operation/date/value, validates confirmation, and pages complete owner-scoped snapshots. Another member or malformed snapshot fails before publication; archived edits remain pending for explicit correction.

elements.title: Master data cache decorators
elements.overview: Wraps band, stage, performance, distance, food, and rating repositories to expose cached reads with source refresh or write-through behavior.

elements.title: Offline operation sync
elements.overview: Coordinates local pending ratings, festival changes, personal history, and schedule locks with remote writes when a session is available.

elements.title: TSV and Room import transaction
elements.overview: Consumer supplied by AppRepositories to local CSV review. Snapshots five existing TSV master files, runs replacement within the supplied WackenDatabase.runInTransaction callback and restores TSV files if the Room transaction fails. Restoration failure reports and preserves the backup path for recovery. It does not issue shared backend writes or turn a successful commit into failure solely for stale backup cleanup.

elements.title: Music identity evidence collector
elements.overview: Implements evidence lookup through existing MusicBrainz and Wikidata HTTP clients plus supplied official-page loader. Artist ID may refine search without renaming canonical band. Loads official pages only after corroborated identity. Optional configured Spotify/YouTube searches provide unverified fallback candidates when primary identity results are empty; credentials are optional and unavailable providers report status. Rate limits/source/page failures remain retryable; adapter never declares candidates trusted.

elements.title: Selected festival rating context
elements.overview: Returns BandRatingContext containing the signed-in member opinion, selected festival planning and after-rating, and retained source provenance. Validates membership in that lineup before reading festival values; wrong user/festival/band results are filtered. Missing selected context stays empty, with no cross-festival fallback.

elements.title: Wacken Planner 2026
elements.description: Android app for shared festival ratings and conflict-aware schedules
elements.overview: Festival attendees rate bands, review a shared schedule, record personal post-show ratings, and retain archived festival history. Admin workflows import lineup CSVs and review band links and metadata. The installed Android process runs UI, use cases, domain rules, adapters, and an on-device Room cache; Supabase supplies authentication and shared data.

elements.title: Room local cache
elements.description: Store lineup and user state on device
elements.overview: Room database, DAOs, entities, and repository adapters keep festival and group data available offline and track pending mutable operations.

elements.title: Android visual theme
elements.description: Apply shared native appearance without replaying work
elements.overview: Provides shared semantic styling for Android screens, including native focused-button outlines, selected rating-choice surfaces and focused selector panels that remain visible in both appearances. Resolves the device-local System, Ironline dark or Field Notes light preference and updates explicitly bound views, panels and system bars in place. Activity lifecycle and preference listeners refresh current appearance and detach on destruction; screen-owned drafts, retained sessions and pending business operations are not reconstructed or executed by restyling. Uses existing private Android SharedPreferences without backend synchronization. Pure palette policy and the controller implement this one presentation responsibility; ADR0024 records the approved design.

flows.title: Archive and establish personal opinions
flows.overview: MainActivity runs the supplied archive use case on a worker. AppRepositories gateway callback first syncs pending ratings and locks and refuses unresolved work. V016 atomically archives and promotes each member final nonempty after-rating; missing/reset retain previous established opinions. After validated acknowledgement, own complete snapshots and festival status publish together under a fresh pending guard. Other-device unsent edits remain pending and require explicit archived correction, rather than silent overwrite.

steps.action: Refuse pending work then call archive
Atomically publish unless new pending work exists

flows.title: Build the shared calendar
flows.overview: An attendee opens the calendar; schedule generation reads performances and applies group conflict rules.

flows.title: Correct own archived assessment
flows.overview: The attendee reviews an exact own archived target/revision, explicitly confirms planning zero-to-five or after one-to-five, and submits a stable operation identity. V017 commits immutable audit and only updates established opinion if this festival is still its current source; planning or older-source changes never promote. Stale reviews require reload. Original recorded date and correction time remain distinct. Newer local pending work blocks cache publication; uncertain remote outcomes retry the same operation.

steps.action: Review exact target then submit operation
Validate own archived target and scale
Commit reviewed revision and immutable audit
Append audit with original and correction dates

flows.title: Create reviewed group festival
flows.overview: An authenticated member reviews uploaded identities and explicitly confirms creation. Cancel leaves no new festival or alias; alias/name conflicts require fresh review. SQL V018 delegates to the existing atomic creation transaction in V015: canonical metadata, lineup and each current member's once-only established-rating planning snapshot commit together; new after-ratings stay empty. The response contains only the creator's planning snapshot. Idempotent retry preserves later edits. A cache failure after shared success is reported separately. Backend behavior is supported by SQL/adapter evidence, not inferred by the Java scanner.

Load exact and suggested identity proposals
Read fresh canonical identities and confirmed aliases
Review nonexact identities with no default selection
Confirm every row and final summary; optionally remember selected aliases
Run the supplier bound by the import screen
Atomically create lineup, confirmed aliases and once-only member planning snapshots
Validate member/festival/lineup acknowledgement and publish creator snapshot
Commit cache together while preserving pending planning edits

flows.title: Delete selected group festival
flows.overview: Active home and archived festival screens share the confirmation dialog. After explicit confirmation, application selection and the authenticated remote adapter delete the chosen festival for the group. Local cleanup runs only after remote acknowledgement and absence check. Remote failure retains local state; local failure after remote success reports sync recovery. SQL V011 and later lifecycle schema preserve canonical bands and established personal history; this flow does not authorize arbitrary deletion or claim production permission testing.

steps.action: Confirm removal of selected festival scope
DELETE selected festival then confirm absence
Apply local cleanup only after remote acknowledgement
Detach retained history and delete selected festival state transactionally

flows.title: Edit selected festival planning
flows.overview: The attendee edits planning for the selected active festival. The detail view stays pinned even if the active festival changes; it validates activity and lineup before delegating to the configured pending-capable planning repository. Planning never changes after-state or established opinions.

steps.action: Validate target and persist pending planning

flows.title: Export own lifecycle and correction audit
flows.overview: Settings exposes legacy ratings CSV, lifecycle version2 and correction audit as separate actions/contracts. Lifecycle records retain established provenance, exact festival planning/after-state, history and audit, preserving missing versus zero and unknown dates. Audit export separates original recorded and correction times; neither export chooses a latest event as an established rating.

flows.title: Review local festival CSV
flows.overview: The admin reviews five optional local CSV files against an active festival snapshot. Only explicitly accepted valid rows are applied, missing companion files remain unchanged, and stale data or combined-reference errors reject publication. This is the TSV fallback/local Room workflow, with no shared-source import API. Canonical catalog records, other festivals, ratings/history and pending work are retained. A Room failure rolls back its transaction and restores TSV backups; restoration failure keeps the backup and reports recovery information.

steps.action: Open retained review with unchecked row choices
Review changes and explicitly apply accepted keys
Revalidate combined data and stale snapshot within supplied transaction
Run replacement in supplied Room transaction with TSV backup protection
Publish accepted master data inside that transaction
Replace local TSV data while preserving canonical catalog
Publish matching Room cache or roll back on failure

flows.title: Rate a festival band
flows.overview: An attendee changes a planning rating from the active lineup; the use case saves it through the configured repository.

flows.title: Record and sync festival after-rating
flows.overview: The attendee records or resets after-state for one member/festival/band. Zero is durable reset, missing is absence; neither promotes an established opinion. Room saves pending operation and nonzero dated history atomically. A later AppRepositories sync pushes explicit operations, skips uncertain legacy facts, acknowledges exact operations and merges complete own snapshots while preserving pending edits.

steps.action: Persist pending fact and nonzero history
Later sync explicit own pending work
Push operation and fetch complete own state

flows.title: Review festival missing music links
flows.overview: Festival admin opens Settings for the active festival. Search selects only lineup bands with missing music fields and never renames them from edited search terms. MusicBrainz/Wikidata corroboration and jointly declared public official-site anchors are facts; the application requires Group identity/name, matching artist ID and a unique canonical platform profile. Optional Spotify/YouTube fallback is explicitly unverified. The user checks source evidence, selects a verified identity and explicitly saves missing links; existing fields and ratings stay unchanged. Cancellation/errors retain saved data and completed reviews for retry. Source-first account-bound save must succeed before cache publication.

steps.action: Search lineup bands with missing fields
Revalidate evidence and current missing fields

flows.title: Review one band music evidence
flows.overview: Band detail opens the same reviewed workflow scoped to one canonical band name. Search terms refine identity only. Unverified or ambiguous results cannot be saved; public lookup may continue across rotation, while cancellation stops unfinished work. The retained repository uses its expected account for shared writes, so account mismatch or save failure must remain unconfirmed. Approval re-evaluates raw evidence/current links and delegates missing-field writes; search ranking and user acknowledgement alone are not verification.

flows.title: Review orphaned pending planning
flows.overview: A sync error carries the exact orphaned pending planning fact. The user may keep it, explicitly move it to active Wacken2026 only when no local or remote target exists, or separately confirm discard. Owner and unchanged-fact checks prevent stale recovery; all failures preserve pending work.

steps.action: Validate owner and unchanged pending fact
For move check remote target absent
Apply explicit safe move or discard
